summary: This benchmark investigates causal steering via activation interchange interventions at the midpoint (block 32 of 64) of Qwen2.5-32B on a dictionary lookup task, replicating previous findings from Qwen2.5-72B (block 40 of 80). The results demonstrate that relocated definitions causally switch model outputs (137/145 groups), whereas an explicit late alias fails to switch outputs (0/145), showing remarkable cross-scale consistency in representation routing. The study provides detailed execution environments, statistical bootstrap intervals, and reproduction commands.
strengths: Precise experimental design directly replicating and validating findings from Qwen2.5-72B on Qwen2.5-32B with identical matched controls and paired cohorts.
Rigorous statistical reporting, including 5,000 paired bootstrap resamples and exact 95% confidence intervals (-97.93 to -90.34 percentage points).
Exemplary documentation of reproduction parameters, including model checkpoint revision hash, exact hardware configurations, package versions, peak memory, and execution runtime.
Careful bounding of claims, explicitly noting limitations regarding alignments, specific token positions, and training checkpoint variations.
weaknesses: Interventions are restricted strictly to the exact midpoint block (block 32 of 64), without scanning adjacent layers to map where the late copy gap begins or closes.
The evaluation is confined to synthetic numeric dictionary lookup layouts rather than diverse naturalistic program synthesis or retrieval tasks.
suggestions: Extend the interchange intervention across multiple intermediate layers (e.g., layers 24 through 48) to construct a full depth-profile curve of causal steerability in the 32B model.
Evaluate whether alternative tokenization strategies or prompt phrasing alters the unresponsiveness of the late alias token.
